# Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion — concept pack

> Source-anchored research for Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion. Run status: COMPLETED.

## Vocabulary

Terms this pack was harvested with, grouped by their relation to the concept; counts are units matched / sources. Zero-hit terms are listed under Coverage. On every unit line, `keywords:` names the terms that matched.

- **self**: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion (21/5)

## Definitions

- [statement] Packed binary byte count is not vector dimensionality: 1024 binary dimensions occupy 128 payload bytes. Preserve the original dimension count in the index; do not set numDimensions to the packed array length. (medium confidence) — https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/embeddings · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://huggingface.co/blog/embedding-quantization, https://github.com/mongodb-developer/vector-quantization

## How it works

- [statement] When only pre-quantized vectors are ingested, MongoDB does not retain an original full-precision copy for automatic rescoring. MongoDB's tutorial recommends retaining a separate float32 field with automatic binary quantization if that rescoring behavior is required; the extra representation belongs in the storage cost model. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://learn.mongodb.com/learn/course/vector-search-performance/vector-search-performance/implementing-quantization · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Generate document and query embeddings with the same model and matching vector dimensions. For pre-quantized fields, serialize the query with the matching BinData element type; full-fidelity queries against int8/int1 fields can return no results without an error. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://learn.mongodb.com/learn/course/vector-search-performance/vector-search-performance/implementing-quantization, https://github.com/mongodb-developer/vector-quantization

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Compared with float32 payload values, scalar int8 uses one quarter of the bytes and packed binary uses one thirty-second. Those arithmetic ratios describe vector values; they do not directly describe total index memory, database storage, or the cluster bill. MongoDB notes that HNSW graph memory does not shrink with the vector values. (medium confidence) — https://huggingface.co/blog/embedding-quantization · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md, https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/bson-binary-vector/bson-binary-vector.md
- [statement] Use driver vector serializers rather than an arbitrary binary blob: the Java example wraps model-returned bytes with BinaryVector.int8Vector(byte[]) or BinaryVector.packedBitVector(byte[], padding). These wrappers tag the vector representation; they do not quantize arbitrary float embeddings. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://github.com/mongodb-developer/vector-quantization · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://dev.to/mongodb/quantize-your-vectors-speed-up-your-java-ai-applications-bng, https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/bson-binary-vector/bson-binary-vector.md
- [statement] For pre-quantized vectors, omit fields.quantization or set it to none. Enabling automatic scalar or binary quantization on int8/int1 BinData can silently skip those vectors instead of indexing them. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md, https://learn.mongodb.com/learn/course/vector-search-performance/vector-search-performance/implementing-quantization
- [statement] For a consolidation TCO estimate, account separately for smaller stored vector payloads, search-index memory, serialization work in ingestion and queries, and any retained float representation. These sources establish possible resource savings but do not establish a measured Atlas-versus-separate-database TCO advantage. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://learn.mongodb.com/learn/course/vector-search-performance/vector-search-performance/implementing-quantization, https://huggingface.co/blog/embedding-quantization
- [statement] Cohere’s Embed API documents int8, uint8, binary, and ubinary outputs alongside floats and permits multiple output types in one request. MongoDB’s available element types still require the application to choose a compatible representation rather than treating every provider dtype as interchangeable. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/embeddings · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/bson-binary-vector/bson-binary-vector.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB can ingest and index model-produced int8 and packed int1 vectors stored as BSON BinData. This stores reduced-precision values in mongod itself, whereas automatic index quantization leaves the original document vectors intact. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://learn.mongodb.com/learn/course/vector-search-performance/vector-search-performance/implementing-quantization
- [statement] BSON vector storage uses binary subtype 9. Its element dtype distinguishes INT8 (0x03), FLOAT32 (0x27), and PACKED_BIT (0x10); a dtype byte and padding byte precede the vector payload. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/bson-binary-vector/bson-binary-vector.md · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion
- [statement] MongoDB's documented pre-quantized int1 ingestion requires dimensions that are multiples of eight and euclidean similarity. Int8 ingestion supports cosine, euclidean, and dotProduct; both support ANN and ENN. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://github.com/mongodb-developer/vector-quantization
- [statement] Cohere provides an upstream producer for quantized ingestion: its Embed API supports explicit int8 and binary/ubinary outputs, and the documentation shows requesting int8 and float together. Provider output must still be serialized into MongoDB's vector format. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/embeddings · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://cohere.com/blog/int8-binary-embeddings, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md
- [statement] Embedding quantization does not preserve retrieval quality uniformly across models. Hugging Face's experiments show model-dependent degradation and stress that scalar calibration ranges affect performance; treating a float-to-int8 cast as equivalent to validated embedding quantization is unsafe. (medium confidence) — https://huggingface.co/blog/embedding-quantization · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://dev.to/mongodb/quantize-your-vectors-speed-up-your-java-ai-applications-bng, https://learn.mongodb.com/learn/course/vector-search-performance/vector-search-performance/implementing-quantization
- [statement] The BSON format permits PACKED_BIT padding from zero through seven bits, while non-packed dtypes require zero padding. That general serialization allowance does not override MongoDB Vector Search's documented multiple-of-eight int1 ingestion requirement. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/bson-binary-vector/bson-binary-vector.md · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md
- [statement] MongoDB supports ingesting and indexing pre-quantized int8 and int1 embeddings as BSON BinData vectors. Quantization occurs before insertion; supported drivers serialize the reduced-precision output into the vector binary format. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://learn.mongodb.com/learn/course/vector-search-performance/vector-search-performance/implementing-quantization
- [statement] BSON vector storage uses binary subtype 9. INT8 (dtype 0x03), FLOAT32 (0x27), and PACKED_BIT (0x10, used for int1) are element types within that subtype, not three separate BSON binary subtype numbers. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/bson-binary-vector/bson-binary-vector.md · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md
- [statement] An INT8 vector stores signed values in [-128,127]. A PACKED_BIT vector groups binary dimensions into bytes; the BSON specification describes these packed byte values as integers in [0,255]. Scalar int8 elements and bytes that pack eight binary dimensions are different representations. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/bson-binary-vector/bson-binary-vector.md · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://huggingface.co/blog/embedding-quantization
- [statement] MongoDB documents euclidean similarity for int1 ingestion, with dimensions a multiple of eight; int8 ingestion supports cosine, euclidean, and dotProduct. The Java example uses euclidean for its packed-bit field. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://github.com/mongodb-developer/vector-quantization
- [statement] The Java example serializes pre-quantized outputs using BinaryVector.int8Vector(byte[]) and BinaryVector.packedBitVector(byte[], padding). MongoDB’s Python examples use Binary.from_vector with BinaryVectorDtype.INT8 or PACKED_BIT. These helpers encode vectors; they do not by themselves calibrate a float-to-int8 quantizer. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb-developer/vector-quantization · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md, https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/bson-binary-vector/bson-binary-vector.md
- [statement] Pre-quantized document storage can reduce mongod disk and WiredTiger footprint as well as mongot index memory. Automatic index quantization instead retains full-precision document embeddings, so the two approaches have different storage cost implications. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://learn.mongodb.com/learn/course/vector-search-performance/vector-search-performance/implementing-quantization
- [statement] Client-side scalar quantization needs consistent calibration ranges: Hugging Face explains that per-dimension calibration buckets affect retrieval performance. MongoDB also describes scalar quantization using per-dimension minimum and maximum ranges. Casting arbitrary floats to integer bytes is therefore not equivalent to a calibrated quantization pipeline. (medium confidence) — https://huggingface.co/blog/embedding-quantization · keywords: Pre-quantized BinData (int8 and int1) ingestion · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/about/vector-quantization.md
